A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MindForge and contain matchable methods and experiments. All pages, including appendices, figures and tables, were available for comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figure 6 report original Minecraft experiments covering task completion, human and agent collaboration, communication rounds and post-collaboration generalization.

after.justification: v3 retains original Minecraft experiments and adds model comparisons and tech-tree progression results in Figure 1b and Table 4.

M1.justification: Reported communication timing changes from forced conversation before any action (v1 Appendix A.2) to predefined initiation after task failure (v3 Sections 4.3 and 6). The core architecture remains. Failure-memory use already appears in v1's action prompt, so its expanded explanation does not establish a new memory component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates dirt and wood collection, including transfer between those tasks. v3 adds extended Minecraft progression involving wooden, stone and iron tools and broader item acquisition (Section 5.5, Figure 1b and Table 4), substantially expanding task requirements beyond single-block collection.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Llama 3.1-8B-powered Voyager to the existing baseline comparison. Table 2 removes the GPT-4-powered MindForge result column, although GPT-4 remains the expert collaborator. Other comparison method families are retained.

E3.justification: The new tech-tree evaluation measures prompting iterations to milestones and distinct items acquired across iterations, extending the design beyond isolated task-completion rates. v3 also introduces Llama 3.1-8B configurations in existing tests and Llama 3.1-70B in the extended evaluation.

E4.justification: v3 adds a collaboration-versus-no-collaboration ablation for tech-tree progression and examines model-size effects. Appendix D supplies explicit perspective-taking traces and replaces the conversation example. The existing communication-round ablation retains its 29%, 42%, 61% and 67% results.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports three-trial averages, ± values and success counts out of three. The 24-trial reporting for isolated tasks remains. The meaning of the ± quantities is unspecified, and no increase in runs for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive tech-tree and item-acquisition results, Llama results, human-assisted Mistral results and PEFT wood-collection results. Table 1 changes Mistral-7B wood completion from 5% to 4%; most retained Mistral/Mixtral collaboration values are unchanged. Figure 7 also changes the illustrated task beliefs: v1 corrects the pickaxe belief to bare-handed mining, while v3 retains pickaxe use across rounds.

T1.justification: Both versions retain the conceptual BDI/BigToM representation. Neither contains formal theorems, proofs or substantive mathematical derivations, and v3 introduces no substantive formal-theory revision.

C1.justification: The three central framework contributions and broad social-learning claim remain. The abstract and conclusion replace the basic-task headline rates with specific claims of 2.3× more unique items and 3× more tech-tree milestones, extending the stated empirical achievements without redefining the central proposal.

C2.justification: The expert-dependence interpretation remains, while v3 adds model-size-based efficiency interpretations and limitations concerning smaller-model hallucinations and transfer across environments/action spaces. v1's text-representation analysis limitation and poor immediate perspective-taking interpretation disappear; its two-task limitation is removed following the broader evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix A adds API providers, model variants, embedding information and DSPy usage, and the introduction points to supplementary code whose contents are unavailable in the supplied PDFs. However, v1's full action, communication, belief and perspective-taking prompts are removed. The fine-tuning description is retained, moving from Appendix B to C.

R1.justification: v3 adds brief comparisons with Adam and Optimus-1 in Section 4 and references for Llama 3, DSPy and Green AI. The related-work section and central positioning around embodied theory of mind and collaborative learning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The experiment narratives, abstract, conclusion and limitations are substantially rewritten. The separate Discussions section disappears while many of its points remain in the experimental narrative. The appendices are reorganized, and the perspective-taking explanation is recast around examples instead of the previous prompt excerpt.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, restructures Tables 1–3 and redraws Figures 4, 5 and 7 with lighter backgrounds and revised text displays. It adds Figure 1b and Table 4 and replaces the appendix prompt display with boxed perspective-taking and conversation examples.

improvement.justification: The tech-tree study addresses v1's explicit two-task limitation and provides useful collaboration controls and repeated-trial results. The overall gain is limited by removal of the full prompts and a weaker qualitative illustration: v1 Figure 7 shows task-belief correction to bare-handed mining, whereas v3 retains the pickaxe belief across rounds.
